en.caption: Island Inhabitants
rows: The Last. Creatures that think they're the last of their kind—perhaps Returned, leonin, or humans—make their home on the island.
First Contact. A prosperous civilization, unconnected to the great poleis, thrives on the island.
Strangers. A species not usually connected to Theros dwells here—such as thri-kreen, yuan-ti, or another creature from the {@book Monster Manual|MM}.
Rivals. Two settlements have turned the island into a war zone.
Prisoner. A powerful monster or dangerous figure from legend is imprisoned on this island.
Tyrant. A powerful individual built a fortress on the island, and all other residents revere them.
Fanatics. The island's residents know only one god and don't appreciate visits from heretics.
The Dead. A settlement of the Returned is located near an obscure passage to the Underworld.
Memories. Everyone on the island is Nyxborn, being the reincarnation of a lost people.
Oracle. An oracle with a reputation for accurate knowledge and prediction lives on the island.

en.caption: Leonin and the Gods
rows: I'm amused by the antics of the gods and their earnest, but ultimately deluded, mortal champions, and I feel smugly superior in my detachment.
The meddling of the gods in mortal affairs makes me angry and bitter. I wish they would just leave us all alone!
I view the gods as worthy adversaries—incredibly clever and well-prepared to play a long game but ultimately doomed to lose their games.
I'm certain every bad thing that happens can ultimately be blamed on the gods, but I roll my eyes at each new twist of fate and try to get on with my life.
I wish that I could be as naive as humans and other mortals who actually think the gods are looking out for them. I miss that kind of innocence.
I don't talk about it among other leonin, but I actually revere the gods and try to please them by my actions.

en.caption: Flesh Warping
rows: The color of the target's hair, eyes, and skin becomes blue, red, yellow, or patterned.
The target's eyes push out of its head at the end of stalks.
The target's hands grow claws, which can be used as daggers.
One of the target's legs grows longer than the other, reducing its walking speed by 10 feet.
The target's eyes become beacons, filling a 15-foot cone with dim light when they are open.
A pair of wings, either feathered or leathery, sprout from the target's back, granting it a flying speed of 30 feet.
The target's ears tear free from its head and scurry away; the target is {@condition deafened}.
Two of the target's teeth turn into short tusks.
The target's skin develops bark-like scales, granting it a +1 bonus to AC but reducing its Charisma score by 2 (to a minimum of 1).
The target's arms and legs switch places, preventing the target from moving unless it crawls.
The target's arms become tentacles with fingers on the ends, increasing its reach by 5 feet.
The target's legs grow incredibly long and springy, increasing its walking speed by 10 feet.
The target grows a long, thin tail, which it can use as a whip.
The target's entire eyes turn black, and it gains {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 120 feet.
The target swells, tripling its weight.
The target becomes thin and skeletal, halving its weight.
The target's head triples in size.
The target's ears become wings, giving it a flying speed of 5 feet.
The target's body becomes unusually brittle, causing the target to have vulnerability to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
The target grows another head, causing it to have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, or {@condition stunned}.

A {@creature beholder} influenced by {@area the Abyss|00b|x} has compound eyes and looks like a floating, cyclopean fly head. It promises not to destroy the characters if they bring it a corpse it has never tasted before.
A dejected {@creature red slaad} wishes to be reunited with its {@creature slaad tadpole}, but it isn't certain where—or in what—it implanted its egg.
A hirsute, axe-wielding {@creature flumph} influenced by {@area Ysgard|04d|x} quests across the land, seeking legendary beasts to slay and epic songs to sing.

en.caption: Outlands Celestials
rows: An {@creature empyrean} calls for aid in taking back a corner of the Outlands overrun by demons.
Wearing grim armor and displaying a rust-colored horn, a {@creature unicorn} influenced by {@area Acheron|010|x} challenges all it encounters to mortal combat.

A fallen {@creature deva}, now neutral aligned, is on permanent vacation. The mellow angel is a font of multiversal secrets, but it shares them only with strangers who prove themselves more relaxed than it.

A {@creature couatl} influenced by {@area Limbo|038|x} has color-changing wings and insists passersby convince it that they're worthy of existing. If the couatl isn't convinced, it has a 50 percent chance of either attacking or wandering off.

rows: {@creature Water Elemental||Water elementals} travel in a group that looks like a long, wandering river.
Some skull-headed {@creature Azer||azers} have been influenced by {@area the Nine Hells|045|x}. They escort a heavily armored caravan of rare ore to the gate-town of Ribcage.
A wounded {@creature mud mephit} asks the characters to help it deliver a sealed package to a leader in a nearby gate-town.

A wealthy {@creature dao} that glistens with gemstones has been influenced by {@area Arborea|015|x}. It leads a parade of glimmering {@creature galeb duhr} between gate-towns as part of a shopping spree for precious rocks.

en.caption: Outlands Fey
rows: Revelers joined a group of {@creature Satyr||satyrs} in their festivities. As the satyrs' celebration has continued for over a year, the revelers seek the characters' help in extricating themselves without offending their hosts.
A kindly {@creature green hag} influenced by {@area Elysium|02a|x} invites passersby to join her for tea in her cottage made of sweets. She makes some of the best cookies in the Outlands.

A pack of {@creature Blink Dog||blink dogs} tracks a band of {@creature Maelephant|MPP|maelephants} (presented {@area later|074|x} in this book) to prevent them from spoiling lands influenced by the Upper Planes.
A gnarled {@creature dryad} influenced by {@area Carceri|026|x} seeks to entrap creatures within the root-snarled, prison-like cavern beneath her grove.
